solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mischievous child, one wielding lasso? That's not right

parts.note: an imp is a naughty youngster
someone who ropes cattle with a lasso

explanation.surface: A naughty child is swinging a lasso about, and a disapproving adult says that is not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper describes behaviour that is unsuitable or incorrect, a close synonym of wrong.

clue.text: Allergen: excessive supply ends in some reaction

indicators.note: ends in asks for the final letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An allergy note: too much of a substance triggers a mild bodily reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is a wheat protein that provokes intolerance or allergic responses in some people.

clue.text: Money: unknown quantity? Small

parts.note: tin is old slang for cash

explanation.surface: A query about finances: an unknown sum of cash, probably a modest one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a common adjective meaning very little in size, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Onset of loud din rising will cause hurt

indicators.note: onset is the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A warning that a loud, growing racket will do physical damage, perhaps to the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or injury to tissue, so it is a hurt in the noun sense.

clue.text: Regularly-performed show wrongly viewed as rare show?

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters of the following words are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A theatre complaint: a staple production is mistakenly billed as a rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke that a familiar old favourite is the opposite of a rare show.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is a well-worn piece in a repertoire, staged or played again and again.

clue.text: Howl when given odd perfume

parts.note: hounds bay, a long howling cry
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: Someone yells in protest on receiving a peculiar-smelling scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is a fragrant lotion distilled from West Indian bay leaves, used as aftershave or cologne.

clue.text: Pollinator beginning to transform vegetable

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An insect visiting crops starts the process that changes a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Beet is a root crop such as beetroot or sugar beet, grown and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Man clutching article is showing uneasiness

indicators.note: clutching means one item holds the others inside it

explanation.surface: A nervous man grips a piece of writing, visibly anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a vague feeling of discomfort or unease, physical or mental.

clue.text: Saw a daughter getting mature

parts.note: D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent notices their daughter growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past tense of see, but here it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, exactly what an adage is.

clue.text: Have another go for the best ever journey, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to try again in pursuit of the greatest trip of all time.
explanation.definitionFit: To retry is to attempt something once more, as a verb phrase for another attempt.

clue.text: Take over popular and successful recording involving Queen?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around and including something else

explanation.surface: A popular chart-topper featuring the band Queen, hinting at assuming a royal throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen suggests the rock band in a recording context, but it is ER, the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive or succeed to something from a predecessor, so to take it over.

clue.text: Writer, eccentric senior person getting allowance

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the following word is jumbled

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A quirky older author receives a regular stipend.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner draws a regular retirement payment from the state or an employer.

clue.text: Rudimentary answer secured by tossing the coin

indicators.note: secured by means held fast within something else
tossing throws things into the air so they land jumbled

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A basic decision is reached by flipping a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just begun and undeveloped, so basic and unformed.

clue.text: Damage memory, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means read the word from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Dwelling on the past can harm one's recollections.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or impair, a direct synonym of the verb damage.

clue.text: Rope, all coiled, before end of key training exercise?

indicators.note: coiled implies twisting round, so the letters are wound into a new order
end of takes just the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A climbing drill: coil all the rope before the essential practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is acting out scenarios, widely used in workplace training sessions; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Dispute line

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noisy quarrel, rhyming with cow
second meaning: a straight rank of things, rhyming with go

explanation.surface: A disagreement about a line, perhaps a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers a quarrel and a straight series of seats or people, with different pronunciations.

clue.text: Our group certainly recalled hosting Liberal church leader

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards
hosting means having a guest inside

explanation.surface: Members of a congregation remember entertaining a progressive clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wesley founded Methodism, so he led a church movement in eighteenth-century England.

clue.text: Religious venue arranged chart deal

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A church organised a contract over a table or plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, a building for worship.

clue.text: Art gallery hosting revolutionary party until now

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest within

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries, the best known in London

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning right round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a do is a social event

explanation.surface: A gallery has been holding a radical political rally right up to the present.
explanation.definitionFit: To date means so far, up to the present moment.

clue.text: Mostly genuine over the German University post

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A real German academic is appointed to a university job.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British university a reader is a senior academic rank just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Reader is a senior British academic rank, a lecturing position just below a professorship.

clue.text: Answer's a lot of relaxation beside small lake

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not every part, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a pond is a little lake

explanation.surface: The solution to stress is plenty of downtime beside a little lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, the verb sense of answer.

clue.text: Automaton dispensing with black base

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A machine sheds its dark foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A root is the base or origin of something, such as the bottom of a tooth or a word's source.

clue.text: Sound of foot soft carpets kept back

indicators.note: kept back suggests moving in the backward direction, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, soft

explanation.surface: Footsteps muffled by plush rugs that are held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp is the heavy noise made by bringing a foot down hard.

clue.text: Very good financial paper in a pale colour?

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
the Financial Times, a respected British business newspaper

explanation.surface: A fine business newspaper printed on tinted paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is famously printed on salmon-pink paper, so the surface hints at its pale colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft colours are muted and gentle, so a soft shade is light and subdued rather than vivid.

clue.text: Set of six deliveries before end of Test? That's obvious

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

indicators.note: end of picks just the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes the last over before a Test match finishes, stating the plain truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown and not hidden, so plain and clear to see.

clue.text: Recalled oily cheese as costly stuff for dressing

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a greasy cheese that served as an expensive salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing suggests salad, beside oily cheese, but it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp lustrous silk fabric used for fine gowns, so costly material for dresses.
